_note: v2 hook overrides for the église. Each painting shows exactly what its hook says. v1 data is untouched.

fr_nef_noun.hook: Linked to "navy" (Latin navis, ship), said NEHF: the long NAVE lined with pews is the 'ship' of the church — a model ship hangs overhead, its deck full of tiny pews.
fr_nef_noun.why: v1 hook (nave lined with pews) did not explain the painted model ship.

fr_cortege_noun.hook: Linked to "cortege", said kor-TEHZH: a slow, solemn CORTÈGE — the bride, the groom and a little page boy holding the train walk up the aisle together.
fr_cortege_noun.why: v1 hook is a funeral; replaced with a gentle, age-appropriate wedding cortège, as painted.

fr_banc_noun.hook: Like "bench", said BAHN: a long wooden PEW (BAHN) with a hot-cross BUN left on its seat.
fr_banc_noun.why: « le banc » here is a church pew; v1 hook is a piggy bank and the source hook is a park bench with a sweet.

fr_basilique_noun.hook: Like "basilica", said bah-zee-LEEK: a grand domed BASILICA rises on the hill beside a giant pot of BASIL.
fr_basilique_noun.why: v1 hook puts the model on a hall shelf; the parvis painting shows it on the hillside.

fr_clochette_noun.hook: Linked to "cloche", said kloh-SHEHT: the church cat's collar carries a SMALL BELL that tinkles as it sits on the square.
fr_clochette_noun.why: Painted as the cat's collar bell, outdoors on the parvis (v1: at the altar).

fr_arcade_noun.hook: Like "arcade", said ahr-KAHD: three pigeons shelter under the stone ARCADE, its arches marching along the square.
fr_arcade_noun.why: The parvis is sunny; rain removed.

fr_eglise_noun.hook: A painted Easter EGG ("ay-GLEEZ") with a little CHURCH on it sits on the church steps.
fr_eglise_noun.why: No church sign is painted; the church is painted on the egg.

fr_chapelle_noun.hook: Close to "chapel", said shah-PEHL: a little stone CHAPEL perched on the hillside above the square.
fr_chapelle_noun.why: Painted on the hill, not in the square.

fr_paroissien_noun.hook: Like "parishioner", said pah-rwah-SYAN: an old PARISHIONER arranges sunflowers in a vase by the pews.
fr_paroissien_noun.why: No font is painted beside him.

fr_vitrail_noun.hook: Linked to "vitreous" (glassy), said vee-TRAHY: a tall STAINED-GLASS WINDOW glowing red, blue and gold — its glass picture even shows a little steam TRAIN.

fr_chemin_de_croix_noun.hook: Linked to "way of the cross", said shuh-man-duh-KRWAH: a framed STATION OF THE CROSS — a little path (chemin) winds up the hill to a cross (croix).
fr_chemin_de_croix_noun.why: One framed station is painted, not fourteen.

fr_transept_noun.hook: Like "transept", said trahn-SEHPT: a little model church shows its TRANSEPT, the two side arms that make the cross shape.
fr_transept_noun.why: Painted as the cross-shaped model church.

fr_encens_noun.hook: Like "incense", said ahn-SAHN: a little brass box of INCENSE grains waits beside the candles.
fr_encens_noun.why: The incense box, not the smoke, carries the hotspot.

fr_sacristie_noun.hook: Like "sacristy", said sah-krees-TEE: a framed picture of the quiet SACRISTY, vestments hanging inside.
fr_sacristie_noun.why: The hotspot is the framed sacristy picture.

fr_etole_noun.hook: Like "stole", said ay-TOL: an embroidered purple STOLE hangs from a hook on the armoire door.
fr_etole_noun.why: No priest is painted (and none is needed).

fr_dalmatique_noun.hook: Like "dalmatic", said dahl-mah-TEEK: a deacon's DALMATIC with wide sleeves — and a spotty DALMATIAN naps beneath it.
